claims.text: The trip record fixes the driver's arrival at 09:47:05 and the cancellation at 09:51:25. That is 260 seconds, forty seconds short of the 300-second free wait. Under POL-NS-21 the driver waits five minutes from arrival at the pickup and only after that may cancel the trip as a rider no-show. The cancelled_after_free_wait flag is false and the wait was not due to end until 09:52:05. The no-show precondition never arose on this trip.

The arrival time the free wait runs from is itself corroborated, not merely asserted: the GPS trace's arrival check reports the nearest fix 2.73 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, on a trace with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum interval of 30 s. Better still for the rider, the driver's first zero-speed fix is at 09:46:50, 15 seconds before the recorded arrival, and the trace holds him stationary at the same spot until 09:51:20. Even measuring the wait from that earliest stationary fix, it would not expire until 09:51:50, and the 09:51:25 cancellation is still premature. On no reading of the trace did the driver complete the free wait.

POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. That condition is the sole source of the charge, and it failed here. The ledger line of 5.00 SGD charged at 09:51:29 (EV-FARE-05054) is therefore unauthorised, and with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00 the rider is still carrying the whole of it. The rider's claim is made out in full: the entire contested 5.00 SGD must be returned, which on POL-GEN-03's vocabulary is FULL_REFUND of the fee charged, with no driver compensation because the fee does not stand.

The driver's counter-statement that he 'waited more than 5 minutes' is contradicted by the platform's own ordering of events. It is not a matter of two accounts in conflict: the arrival event, the wait-timer event, the cancellation event and the fee event are all carried on one COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0, and the arithmetic between arrival and cancellation is 260 seconds. The rider's account — cancelled about four minutes after arrival — is the one the record supports.

I do not dispute that the driver satisfied the POL-NS-23 contact obligation: two in-app messages (09:47:30 and 09:49:50) and one in-app call placed at 09:50:30, all before the 09:51:25 cancellation, so message_count and call_count are both non-zero. But POL-NS-23 governs contact only. It is a separate requirement that does not shorten, waive or excuse the POL-NS-21 free wait, and the driver's compliance with it cannot convert a cancellation made inside the free wait into a lawful no-show.

There is no POL-GEN-26 gap here and escalation is not open. Every fact the operative rules need — when the driver arrived and when he cancelled — is carried on COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, and the sole absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-05054-01, is a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY with status MISSING and weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); no no-show clause requires a traffic record, POL-NS-21 requiring trip_record and gps_trace and POL-NS-22 requiring fare_breakdown, all three of which are present and unimpaired. The absence of a document nobody needs is not an open question.

claims.text: The driver's arrival at the pickup at 09:47:05 is corroborated by the GPS trace, so POL-NS-21's free-wait clock started with the driver physically on the spot: 22 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s, every fix reporting horizontal accuracy (max 9 m), and the nearest fix 2.73 m from the pickup point, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (arrival_check.corroborated = true). No version of the rider's case can contend the driver never turned up.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met in full, which closes the rider's most direct route to a refund: the driver sent two in-app messages (09:47:30 and 09:49:50, both read by the rider at 09:48:03 and 09:50:17 on the chat log) and placed an in-app call at 09:50:30 that rang 22 s unanswered, both limbs falling before trip_record.cancelled_at 09:51:25 (derived contact_before_cancel.obligation_met = true). POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the message or the call is missing; neither is.

Far from abandoning the pickup, the driver sat at it: every fix from 09:46:50 to 09:51:20 reports speed 0 kph at the pickup (about 1.3194, 103.7635) and the whole 1.34 km of trace distance was spent on the approach. The pickup presence that the POL-NS-21 free wait exists to secure was in fact given, alongside two messages and a call to the rider.

The rider's account, that she 'was already walking down', is carried by nothing in the record: the trace attached to this trip contains no rider track at all (rider_track is empty), and the chat log contains no message from the rider even though she read both of the driver's. The driver does not ask the judge to infer from that absence that she was not coming, because POL-GEN-26 forbids an outcome being inferred from missing evidence; the point is that under POL-GEN-25 an assertion resting on no evidence id cannot be weighed against the driver's account, which is carried by artifacts at full admissibility weight.

The only provisions on a no-show that hand money back to the rider are POL-NS-23 (message or call not attempted) and POL-NS-24 (driver late to the pickup and no contact attempted). Neither is engaged here: the driver messaged and called, and he arrived at 09:47:05. The rider's request for the 5.00 SGD therefore rests on no clause that grants it, and under POL-GEN-03 an outcome issues on the contested amount only as a rule provides.

The driver does not press the wait arithmetic as his own statement has it, and the judge should know where that statement is overstated: the trip record shows arrival at 09:47:05 and cancellation at 09:51:25, 260 s, against a POL-NS-21 free wait of 300 s running to 09:52:05 (cancelled_after_free_wait = false), so the counterparty statement that he 'waited more than 5 minutes' is not borne out on the wait, although its other two elements, the message and the call, are exactly what the record shows. The driver does not ask the judge to read 260 s as 300 s; he asks only that the 40-second timing error be confined to the fee if the fee falls at all, and not be converted into anything further against him.

If anything is returned, the rider's recovery cannot exceed the fee charged. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is conditional on the driver both failing to arrive by the pickup deadline and failing to attempt contact; the driver arrived and attempted contact, so that limb is not engaged and no credit arises. The fee charged (5.00 SGD) also matches the fee POL-NS-22 sets, so no referral on the amount arises either.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the arithmetic, and the platform's own record settles it. The driver arrived at the pickup at 09:47:05 (EV-TRIP-05054, corroborated by the GPS trace EV-GPS-05054, whose nearest fix is 2.73 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius) and cancelled at 09:51:25 — 260 seconds later. Under POL-NS-21 the free wait runs for 300 seconds (5 minutes) from the driver's arrival, i.e. to 09:52:05, and the record's own flag confirms cancelled_after_free_wait = false. POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD no-show fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. That condition was not met, so the 5.00 SGD charged at 09:51:29 (EV-FARE-05054; refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider still carries the whole of it) was not authorised and must be returned. The rider is owed the entire contested sum: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with driver_compensation_sgd null. The driver's counter-statement that he 'waited more than 5 minutes' is not borne out on the wait, and the driver's own submission concedes the 260-second figure; the 40-second shortfall is what voids the fee, and nothing further is taken from the driver beyond losing the fee.

On the driver's other points: his contact obligation under POL-NS-23 was in fact met — two in-app messages (09:47:30 and 09:49:50) and one in-app call (09:50:30, unanswered after 22 s), all before the 09:51:25 cancellation — so the fee is not voided on that ground. But POL-NS-23 governs contact only; it does not shorten, waive or excuse the POL-NS-21 free wait, and it cannot convert a cancellation made inside the free wait into a lawful no-show. His submission that the rider's refund 'rests on no clause' is rejected: the refund flows from POL-NS-22's own precondition failing together with POL-NS-21's free wait.

The rider's argument that the wait should be measured from the first stationary fix (09:46:50) is not the policy's start — the free wait starts from trip_record.arrived_at, settled as 09:47:05 — but it makes no difference: even measured from 09:46:50 the wait would not expire until 09:51:50, still after the 09:51:25 cancellation. The rider's statement that she was 'already walking down' is carried by no artifact (the trace carries no rider track and the chat log carries no rider message), and the driver's point that it rests on no evidence is noted, but the outcome does not turn on it.

No referral arises. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit requires both a failure to arrive by the deadline and a failure to attempt contact; the driver arrived and attempted contact, so it is not engaged. The fee charged (5.00 SGD) matches the fee POL-NS-22 sets, so no referral on the amount arises. The rider's no-show count is below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3, so no repeat-no-show flag arises. POL-GEN-26 escalation is not open: every fact these rules need is carried on COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, and the only absent artifact (EV-ADVIS-05054-01, a traffic advisory, weight 0.0) is required by no no-show clause. The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band with no fraud flag, so this ruling is final at any confidence.

To the rider and the driver: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged on this trip was not authorised, and the rider is refunded it in full.

POL-NS-21 gives the driver a free wait of 300 seconds (5 minutes) running from his arrival at the pickup, and only after that may he cancel the trip as a rider no-show. The record fixes the arrival at 09:47:05 and the cancellation at 09:51:25 — 260 seconds, with the trip record's own cancelled_after_free_wait flag false and the wait not due to end until 09:52:05. That arrival is not merely asserted: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05054) corroborates it, the nearest fix 2.73 m from the pickup inside the 50 m STANDARD radius on a complete trace with no gaps. Even measuring from the driver's earliest stationary fix at 09:46:50, the wait would be 275 seconds, still short. So the free wait was not completed on any reading.

POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. That precondition is the sole source of the charge and it failed, so the 5.00 SGD charged at 09:51:29 (EV-FARE-05054, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is not owed and is returned in whole. This is FULL_REFUND of the contested 5.00 SGD, with no driver compensation.

The driver's points are largely correct and I accept them, but they do not save the fee. His arrival is corroborated; he did sit stationary at the pickup; and his POL-NS-23 contact obligation was met in full — two in-app messages at 09:47:30 and 09:49:50 (both read) and a call at 09:50:30, all before the 09:51:25 cancellation. POL-NS-23, however, governs contact only: it neither shortens nor waives the free wait in POL-NS-21. I also accept the driver's own correction that his written statement he 'waited more than 5 minutes' is not borne out — the arithmetic is 260 seconds — and that error is confined to the fee, nothing further is drawn from it. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise, because the driver did arrive and did attempt contact, and the rider's assertion that she was 'already walking down' rests on no artifact (the trace carries no rider track), so nothing is inferred from it either way.

The remaining claims are answered on the same facts. The rider's argument that POL-NS-23 compliance cannot cure a cancellation made inside the free wait is accepted, and it is decisive here — not through POL-NS-23 or POL-NS-24, but through POL-NS-22's own precondition. The driver's argument that only POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-24 return money is rejected: POL-NS-22 is itself a rule that grants nothing unless the free wait has elapsed, and it had not.

No referral arises. POL-NS-22's referral fires only where the amount charged differs from its 5.00 SGD fee, and the ledger charged exactly 5.00 SGD (fee_matches_policy true). POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag counts this trip only if its fee stands; the fee does not stand, and the counter is not present on the profile in any event. No escalation is open: every fact the operative rules need is carried on COMPLETE artifacts at full weight, and the single absent artifact (EV-ADVIS-05054-01, a traffic advisory) is required by no no-show clause, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. The disputed amount (5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band) makes this ruling final. The deciding facts are carried by EV-TRIP-05054 and EV-GPS-05054, both at weight 1.0, so confidence is placed at 0.95.

ledger.claim: The trip record fixes the driver's arrival at 09:47:05 and the cancellation at 09:51:25. That is 260 seconds, forty seconds short of the 300-second free wait. Under POL-NS-21 the driver waits five minutes from arrival at the pickup and only after that may cancel the trip as a rider no-show. The cancelled_after_free_wait flag is false and the wait was not due to end until 09:52:05. The no-show precondition never arose on this trip.

The arrival time the free wait runs from is itself corroborated, not merely asserted: the GPS trace's arrival check reports the nearest fix 2.73 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, on a trace with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum interval of 30 s. Better still for the rider, the driver's first zero-speed fix is at 09:46:50, 15 seconds before the recorded arrival, and the trace holds him stationary at the same spot until 09:51:20. Even measuring the wait from that earliest stationary fix, it would not expire until 09:51:50, and the 09:51:25 cancellation is still premature. On no reading of the trace did the driver complete the free wait.

POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. That condition is the sole source of the charge, and it failed here. The ledger line of 5.00 SGD charged at 09:51:29 (EV-FARE-05054) is therefore unauthorised, and with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00 the rider is still carrying the whole of it. The rider's claim is made out in full: the entire contested 5.00 SGD must be returned, which on POL-GEN-03's vocabulary is FULL_REFUND of the fee charged, with no driver compensation because the fee does not stand.

The driver's counter-statement that he 'waited more than 5 minutes' is contradicted by the platform's own ordering of events. It is not a matter of two accounts in conflict: the arrival event, the wait-timer event, the cancellation event and the fee event are all carried on one COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0, and the arithmetic between arrival and cancellation is 260 seconds. The rider's account — cancelled about four minutes after arrival — is the one the record supports.

I do not dispute that the driver satisfied the POL-NS-23 contact obligation: two in-app messages (09:47:30 and 09:49:50) and one in-app call placed at 09:50:30, all before the 09:51:25 cancellation, so message_count and call_count are both non-zero. But POL-NS-23 governs contact only. It is a separate requirement that does not shorten, waive or excuse the POL-NS-21 free wait, and the driver's compliance with it cannot convert a cancellation made inside the free wait into a lawful no-show.

There is no POL-GEN-26 gap here and escalation is not open. Every fact the operative rules need — when the driver arrived and when he cancelled — is carried on COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, and the sole absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-05054-01, is a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY with status MISSING and weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); no no-show clause requires a traffic record, POL-NS-21 requiring trip_record and gps_trace and POL-NS-22 requiring fare_breakdown, all three of which are present and unimpaired. The absence of a document nobody needs is not an open question.

The driver's arrival at the pickup at 09:47:05 is corroborated by the GPS trace, so POL-NS-21's free-wait clock started with the driver physically on the spot: 22 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s, every fix reporting horizontal accuracy (max 9 m), and the nearest fix 2.73 m from the pickup point, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (arrival_check.corroborated = true). No version of the rider's case can contend the driver never turned up.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met in full, which closes the rider's most direct route to a refund: the driver sent two in-app messages (09:47:30 and 09:49:50, both read by the rider at 09:48:03 and 09:50:17 on the chat log) and placed an in-app call at 09:50:30 that rang 22 s unanswered, both limbs falling before trip_record.cancelled_at 09:51:25 (derived contact_before_cancel.obligation_met = true). POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the message or the call is missing; neither is.

Far from abandoning the pickup, the driver sat at it: every fix from 09:46:50 to 09:51:20 reports speed 0 kph at the pickup (about 1.3194, 103.7635) and the whole 1.34 km of trace distance was spent on the approach. The pickup presence that the POL-NS-21 free wait exists to secure was in fact given, alongside two messages and a call to the rider.

The rider's account, that she 'was already walking down', is carried by nothing in the record: the trace attached to this trip contains no rider track at all (rider_track is empty), and the chat log contains no message from the rider even though she read both of the driver's. The driver does not ask the judge to infer from that absence that she was not coming, because POL-GEN-26 forbids an outcome being inferred from missing evidence; the point is that under POL-GEN-25 an assertion resting on no evidence id cannot be weighed against the driver's account, which is carried by artifacts at full admissibility weight.

The only provisions on a no-show that hand money back to the rider are POL-NS-23 (message or call not attempted) and POL-NS-24 (driver late to the pickup and no contact attempted). Neither is engaged here: the driver messaged and called, and he arrived at 09:47:05. The rider's request for the 5.00 SGD therefore rests on no clause that grants it, and under POL-GEN-03 an outcome issues on the contested amount only as a rule provides.

The driver does not press the wait arithmetic as his own statement has it, and the judge should know where that statement is overstated: the trip record shows arrival at 09:47:05 and cancellation at 09:51:25, 260 s, against a POL-NS-21 free wait of 300 s running to 09:52:05 (cancelled_after_free_wait = false), so the counterparty statement that he 'waited more than 5 minutes' is not borne out on the wait, although its other two elements, the message and the call, are exactly what the record shows. The driver does not ask the judge to read 260 s as 300 s; he asks only that the 40-second timing error be confined to the fee if the fee falls at all, and not be converted into anything further against him.

If anything is returned, the rider's recovery cannot exceed the fee charged. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is conditional on the driver both failing to arrive by the pickup deadline and failing to attempt contact; the driver arrived and attempted contact, so that limb is not engaged and no credit arises. The fee charged (5.00 SGD) also matches the fee POL-NS-22 sets, so no referral on the amount arises either.
